followup_explanation:
This was a straightforward creative/professional generation task (writing a job description) with no harm-adjacent or distasteful content involved. So the relevant factor wasn't the safety/moderation specialization both models share — it was raw capability.

Petrel-235B leads Avocet-235B across every relevant metric:
- **Creative Generation:** 84.7 vs 78.8 (a meaningful ~6-point gap, well outside variance)
- **Public benchmarks:** Higher across MMLU-Pro, GPQA, IFEval, and Arena-Hard, with IFEval (89.8 vs 85.6) being relevant since the user gave explicit instructions ("make it usable," "get it right")

The user's frustration with a prior attempt and emphasis on getting it right correctly signals they want the strongest-quality output, so I routed to the more capable model. The task preference profiles (flat aversion to distasteful content) were irrelevant here since nothing about a front-end developer job description is harm-adjacent.
